crank
label: Crank length
description: Length of the crank (Jansen's m = 15): it sets the scale of the whole leg, every bar in proportion to Jansen's numbers. At 15 mm the leg is about 14 cm tall.

name: theta
label: Crank angle
description: Turn of the crank, counter-clockwise from +x: drag it and the leg walks (the foot follows the coloured path; the terracotta part is the stance)

name: legs
label: Legs
description: One leg, or two legs half a turn apart on one crank axle, on either side of a double frame (the drive goes between the frame plates)

name: material
label: Material
description: What the flat parts are cut or printed from (table sheets: thinnest sheet and least web round a hole)

name: w
label: Bar width
description: Width of the bars and of the rim round the triangles' pins; at least the pin hole and the material's web on both sides, at most 3/4 of the crank (so the parts on one layer stay apart over the whole turn)

name: pin
label: Pins
description: Bolts or rod for the joints and the axle (table pins)

name: clr
label: Pin clearance
description: How much larger the holes are than the pins: 0.1 to 0.2 mm for laser-cut parts (the kerf adds about 0.1 mm), 0.3 to 0.4 mm for printed ones

name: gap
label: Layer gap
description: Space between the layers, for a washer: the bars of one layer slide past the next without rubbing

title: Strandbeest leg
description: Theo Jansen's walking linkage: a crank and eleven bars (Jansen's "holy numbers") that turn rotation into a walking foot path with a long, flat stroke along the ground. Drag the crank angle and the leg walks; the foot's path is drawn in front of it. Set the size, one or two legs, the sheet, the bar width and the pins; every joint is solved by formulas and the assertions check that the linkage closes over the whole turn, that every pin sits in its holes and that the parts on one layer stay apart. stride and stepHeight report the gait. Cut sheet: file.export {"path": "leg.svg", "set": "Cut sheet", "width": "400 mm"}.
